Subject: [PATCH] KVM: MTRR: fix kvm_mtrr_check_gfn_range_consistency page
 fault

The following #PF may occurs:
[ 1403.317041] BUG: unable to handle kernel paging request at 0000000200000068
[ 1403.317045] IP: [<ffffffffc04c20b0>] __mtrr_lookup_var_next+0x10/0xa0 [kvm]

[ 1403.317123] Call Trace:
[ 1403.317134]  [<ffffffffc04c2a65>] ? kvm_mtrr_check_gfn_range_consistency+0xc5/0x120 [kvm]

[ 1403.317171]  [<ffffffffc04c04e4>] ? kvm_cpuid+0x34/0x190 [kvm]
[ 1403.317180]  [<ffffffffc04a5bb9>] ? kvm_mmu_page_fault+0x59/0xe0 [kvm]
[ 1403.317183]  [<ffffffffc0d729e1>] ? vmx_handle_exit+0x1d1/0x14a0 [kvm_intel]

[ 1403.317213]  [<ffffffffc0487eb6>] ? kvm_vcpu_ioctl+0x316/0x5d0 [kvm]
[ 1403.317215]  [<ffffffff81088225>] ? do_sigtimedwait+0xd5/0x220
[ 1403.317217]  [<ffffffff811f84dd>] ? do_vfs_ioctl+0x9d/0x5c0
[ 1403.317224]  [<ffffffffc04928ae>] ? kvm_on_user_return+0x3e/0x70 [kvm]
[ 1403.317225]  [<ffffffff811f8a74>] ? SyS_ioctl+0x74/0x80
[ 1403.317227]  [<ffffffff815bf0b6>] ? entry_SYSCALL_64_fastpath+0x1e/0xa8
[ 1403.317242] RIP  [<ffffffffc04c20b0>] __mtrr_lookup_var_next+0x10/0xa0 [kvm]

At mtrr_lookup_fixed_next(), when the condition
'if (iter->index >= ARRAY_SIZE(iter->mtrr_state->fixed_ranges))' becomes true,
mtrr_lookup_var_start() is called with iter->range with gargabe values from the
fixed MTRR union field. Then, list_prepare_entry() do not call list_entry()
initialization, keeping a garbage pointer in iter->range which is accessed in
the following __mtrr_lookup_var_next() call.

Fixes: f571c0973e4b8c888e049b6842e4b4f93b5c609c
Signed-off-by: Alexis Dambricourt <alexis@blade-group.com>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Paolo Bonzini <pbonzini@redhat.com>

diff --git a/arch/x86/kvm/mtrr.c b/arch/x86/kvm/mtrr.c
index c146f3c262c3..0149ac59c273 100644
--- a/arch/x86/kvm/mtrr.c
+++ b/arch/x86/kvm/mtrr.c
@@ -539,6 +539,7 @@ static void mtrr_lookup_var_start(struct mtrr_iter *iter)
 
 	iter->fixed = false;
 	iter->start_max = iter->start;
+	iter->range = NULL;
 	iter->range = list_prepare_entry(iter->range, &mtrr_state->head, node);
 
 	__mtrr_lookup_var_next(iter);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `arch/x86/kvm/mtrr.c`**
   - A new line was added to initialize `iter->range` to `NULL` before it is used in the `list_prepare_entry()` function. This change ensures that `iter->range` does not contain garbage values when it is accessed later in the `__mtrr_lookup_var_next()` function.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modification in `arch/x86/kvm/mtrr.c` addresses a bug that could lead to a kernel page fault due to uninitialized memory. By initializing `iter->range` to `NULL`, the patch prevents the use of garbage values that could occur if the condition `if (iter->index >= ARRAY_SIZE(iter->mtrr_state->fixed_ranges))` is true. This change ensures that the subsequent function call to `__mtrr_lookup_var_next()` operates on a valid state, thereby improving the stability and reliability of the KVM MTRR handling.

Here is the root cause:
The bug occurs when the condition `if (iter->index >= ARRAY_SIZE(iter->mtrr_state->fixed_ranges))` is true, leading to the call of `mtrr_lookup_var_start()` with `iter->range` containing garbage values from the fixed MTRR union field. This results in an uninitialized pointer being accessed in the subsequent `__mtrr_lookup_var_next()` function, causing a kernel page fault.

Here is the patch:
 
 static void mtrr_lookup_var_start(struct mtrr_iter *iter)
 {
 	struct kvm_mtrr *mtrr_state = iter->mtrr_state;
 
 	iter->fixed = false;
 	iter->start_max = iter->start;
+	iter->range = NULL;
 	iter->range = list_prepare_entry(iter->range, &mtrr_state->head, node);
 
 	__mtrr_lookup_var_next(iter);
 }

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
if (iter->index >= ARRAY_SIZE(iter->mtrr_state->fixed_ranges))
mtrr_lookup_var_start(iter);
```
Reason:
When the condition `if (iter->index >= ARRAY_SIZE(iter->mtrr_state->fixed_ranges))` is true, `mtrr_lookup_var_start()` is called with `iter->range` containing garbage values from the fixed MTRR union field. This leads to an uninitialized pointer being accessed in the subsequent `__mtrr_lookup_var_next()` function, causing a kernel page fault.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
iter->range = NULL;
iter->range = list_prepare_entry(iter->range, &mtrr_state->head, node);
```
Reason:
By initializing `iter->range` to `NULL` before calling `list_prepare_entry()`, the code ensures that any garbage pointer is cleared, preventing the access of an uninitialized pointer in the subsequent function call. This effectively avoids the kernel page fault.
